title: Expeditionary Logistics Instructor (MGySgt to GySgt) NMOS (0451, 0491, 1371, 2181, 3043, 3537), DC I&L
raw_text:
8. MOS 0477, Expeditionary Logistics Instructor (MGySgt to GySgt) NMOS
(0451, 0491, 1371, 2181, 3043, 3537), DC I&L

    a. Summary. Expeditionary Logistics Instructors (ELIs) support
commanders by being skilled in the art and science of command and control and
the logistics operations cycle, which is defined as a continuous process used
to plan logistics operations, receive and validate logistics requests, task
subordinate units to execute logistics missions, and define requirements to
tactical level headquarters and operational level logistics activities. ELIs
are capable of integrating the functional areas of logistics with the other
warfighting functions during planning, and while executing naval
expeditionary force (NEF) logistics operations in complex environments,
proficient in training design and can implement and manage unit readiness
planning (URP), effective operational planning team (OPT) leaders, and
proponents of standardization in procedures and training. MOS 0477 will be
assigned upon successful completion of the Advanced Expeditionary Logistics
Operations Course (AXLOC) (M09F2F9).

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     secret level clearance.

            (2) Career Level School completion (resident or nonresident).

    c. Requirements. Completion of the Advanced Expeditionary Logistics
Operations Course (AXLOC) (M09F2F9).

       d.   Duties

        (1) Design, conduct, supervise, and validate staff and unit training
plans in accordance with the unit commander’s guidance, higher headquarters
plans, and applicable Marine Corps orders.

        (2) Evaluate and assess all unit readiness data submitted in the
Defense Readiness Reporting System.

        (3) Validate unit operations, training, and readiness standing
operating procedures and ensure alignment with higher headquarters plans and
applicable Marine Corps orders.

        (4) Submit recommended changes to training standards and doctrine
through the appropriate chain of command.

        (5) Develop and implement concepts of operations and concepts of
logistics support.

            (6) Provide instruction on the Marine Corps planning process and lead
OPTs.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
